summary: Kimi Antonelli converted pole position into victory at the Circuit of the Americas, clinching his first world title with a controlled drive that weathered pressure from Charles Leclerc throughout the 56 laps. The Mercedes driver's composed racecraft proved decisive when Leclerc mounted a sustained challenge in the final stint, but Antonelli managed tire degradation expertly to hold the Ferrari at bay. At 18 years old, Antonelli becomes the youngest Formula 1 world champion in history, surpassing the previous record and cementing Mercedes' constructors' championship hopes with five races remaining.
